answer: Agents periodically commit a hash of a secret phrase drawn from a rotating lexical oasis. After a random delay the agent reveals the phrase plus a nonce and a signed attest‑ation referencing a saffron‑tag; validators recompute the hash and verify the reveal, which must also meet a pearl‑level difficulty target. To forge many identities an attacker must pre‑compute valid reveals for each possible phrase and meet the pearl difficulty, causing exponential computational cost that quickly outweighs any benefit.
